# Future Goals

Graduating in April 2026 with a clear sense of where I want to go, professionally and personally. The next twelve months break into three deliberate phases: graduate, travel, then move to London and start working. Here is what I am working towards in each.

## Career

```{=html}
<div class="fg-career">

  <div class="fg-career__card">
    <div class="fg-career__eyebrow">Short term · 6 to 12 months out</div>
    <div class="fg-career__title">Business analyst in the gaming industry</div>
    <div class="fg-career__body">My goal after graduation is a business analyst role in gaming. It is a sector where analytical thinking shapes real product decisions: live-service economies, player retention modelling, monetisation experiments, content release pipelines. The combination of fast-moving product cycles and rich behavioural datasets is exactly the environment I want to operate in early in my career, and the analytical patterns I worked through in my Online Shoppers research paper (cost-sensitive thresholding, threshold-versus-classifier trade-offs) translate directly to the kind of retention and conversion problems gaming analysts work on every day.</div>
  </div>

  <div class="fg-career__card">
    <div class="fg-career__eyebrow">Location · Late 2026 onward</div>
    <div class="fg-career__title">Working abroad in London</div>
    <div class="fg-career__body">London is one of Europe's largest hubs for both gaming and broader analytics work. Relocating after graduation means access to the network, the pace and the role density that early career growth depends on. The intention is to land in London by late 2026 and treat the first twelve months there as deliberately steep: the kind of role where the person sitting next to you knows things you do not, and the gap is the point.</div>
  </div>

</div>
```

## Travel

The summer between graduation and starting full-time work is the rare window where a long, multi-region trip is genuinely possible. I am using it. The itinerary covers East Asia (Hong Kong, mainland China, South Korea), Southeast Asia (Vietnam) and the United States East Coast (Miami, New York), spread across roughly three months. The map below is the actual route.

```{python}
#| label: fig-travel-map
#| fig-cap: "Summer 2026 itinerary across six destinations and three regions. East Asia leg covers Hong Kong, southern mainland China and Seoul; Southeast Asia leg covers Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City); Americas leg covers Miami and New York. Hover any marker to see what I am most looking forward to in each."

import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go

destinations = pd.DataFrame({
    "City":      ["Hong Kong",  "Shanghai",   "Seoul",       "Hanoi",       "Miami",      "New York"],
    "Country":   ["China",      "China",      "South Korea", "Vietnam",     "USA",        "USA"],
    "Region":    ["East Asia",  "East Asia",  "East Asia",   "SE Asia",     "Americas",   "Americas"],
    "Lat":       [22.3193,      31.2304,      37.5665,       21.0285,       25.7617,      40.7128],
    "Lon":       [114.1694,     121.4737,     126.9780,      105.8542,     -80.1918,     -74.0060],
    "Order":     [1,            2,            3,             4,             5,            6],
    "Highlight": [
        "Dim sum, Victoria Peak views, the density of street life in Mong Kok",
        "Pudong skyline by night, the contrast between the Bund and the back streets",
        "Hanok villages in Bukchon, Korean barbecue at source, the design culture",
        "Pho 24/7, the motorbike chaos of Hanoi, the limestone karsts of Halong Bay",
        "Cuban food in Little Havana, art deco in South Beach, sunsets over the Atlantic",
        "Walking Manhattan end-to-end, jazz in Greenwich Village, the New York pace itself",
    ],
})

region_colours = {
    "East Asia": "#c8102e",
    "SE Asia":   "#1e7e34",
    "Americas":  "#0a579c",
}

fig = go.Figure()

# Connection lines between consecutive destinations
fig.add_trace(go.Scattergeo(
    lon=destinations["Lon"],
    lat=destinations["Lat"],
    mode="lines",
    line=dict(width=1.5, color="#888", dash="dot"),
    hoverinfo="skip",
    showlegend=False,
))

# Markers per region
for region, colour in region_colours.items():
    subset = destinations[destinations["Region"] == region]
    fig.add_trace(go.Scattergeo(
        lon=subset["Lon"],
        lat=subset["Lat"],
        mode="markers+text",
        marker=dict(size=14, color=colour, line=dict(width=2, color="white")),
        text=subset["City"],
        textposition="top center",
        textfont=dict(size=12, color="#1a1a1a", family="Inter, sans-serif"),
        name=region,
        hovertemplate=(
            "<b>%{text}</b><br>" +
            "<i>" + subset["Country"] + "</i><br>" +
            "Stop %{customdata[0]} of 6<br><br>" +
            "%{customdata[1]}<extra></extra>"
        ),
        customdata=subset[["Order", "Highlight"]].values,
    ))

fig.update_geos(
    showcountries=True, countrycolor="#bbb",
    showcoastlines=True, coastlinecolor="#999",
    showland=True, landcolor="#f7f7f7",
    showocean=True, oceancolor="#e8eef2",
    projection_type="natural earth",
    lataxis_range=[-10, 60],
    lonaxis_range=[-100, 145],
)

fig.update_layout(
    height=520,
    margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=10, b=10),
    paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    font=dict(family="Inter, sans-serif", color="#1a1a1a"),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=-0.05, x=0, bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)"),
)
fig.show()
```

## What I want to bring back

```{=html}

A few weeks of forced immersion is a more efficient way to push my Spanish from intermediate toward upper-intermediate than another six months of textbook study.</div>

    <div class="fg-bring-back__body">Travel is the most efficient mechanism for building relationships outside your existing network. Even a small set of contacts in each region is a structural advantage in a career where remote and cross-region work is increasingly the norm.</div>
```
